definition: A disruptive E.L.F. that causes malfunction, interference, and chaos in whatever system it inhabits. Named after WWII aviation folklore. Gremlins are the most commonly reported E.L.F. type because people notice when things go wrong.
origin: E.L.F. classification — from World War II folklore of spirits sabotaging aircraft
example: There's a gremlin in the building's grid. Power drops every night at 0200. Maintenance can't find the fault because there isn't one.
